S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report any thermal incident involving fire, injury, emergency-service response, property damage, or a unit safety shutdown to the regulator within 5 business days after learning of it. Any fatality, serious injury, or continuing imminent hazard must be reported to the regulator within 24 hours. Manufacturers must notify affected customers promptly when an incident indicates a material risk to their units, and provide interim safe-use or isolation instructions where appropriate.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C before market entry and at least annually thereafter, using a regulator-approved protocol and representative production units. Manufacturers must submit per-model results, including failure rates, to the regulator and disclose those results to current and prospective customers of that model in a clear, accessible format. A failure rate above 5% requires prompt regulator notification and a corrective-action plan within 60 days; it does not by itself prohibit sale.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New units manufactured 24 months after this standard takes effect must support remote emergency shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized activation and a locally accessible alternative. For units already installed on that date, manufacturers must provide a retrofit or equivalent safe remedy within 6 years where technically feasible, and give owners clear instructions for emergency isolation in the interim.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New units manufactured 36 months after this standard takes effect must include built-in fire suppression meeting a regulator-approved performance and reliability protocol.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A recall is mandatory when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed unit-years over a rolling 12-month period, or when the regulator determines a defect presents an imminent serious safety risk. Manufacturers must notify the regulator and affected customers without delay, explain the risk and remedy, and provide status updates until the remedy is complete.

document.section_notes: Final rules adopt serious-incident reporting with 5-business-day general and 24-hour serious deadlines, but scope is serious-only. S2 requires 55 °C testing and customer disclosure of per-model failure rates, yet a >5% failure rate triggers only corrective action, not a sales stop. S3 delays new-unit shut-off to 24 months and gives a 6-year retrofit window; S4 requires built-in suppression at 36 months; S5 mandates recall at 8/100k with immediate notices and no phase-in.
